title: `baselines.phusdMinterMask` is the one write-once baseline with no resume abort, so a resume leg silently re-derives a POST-cutover mask and the two-sided delta self-certifies
originBasis: Exact fingerprint afe63747… absent. Semantic sweep of the write-once-baseline family (4fd1642310, 80a741a27f) confirms dedup's SEPARATE ruling on both axes; see relatedFindings. entryPoint promotion-ready:resume is COLD. NEW.
description: The suite now carries three write-once baselines. Two are mechanically protected against a hand-trimmed progress file: `bptAtCutover` (story 074) and `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover`, whose Phase 0 has an explicit `require(!_isConfigured("p4e_migrate") || phlimboBaselineFromProgressFile, "RESUME ABORT: ...")` at :798-801, precisely because re-deriving it from an emptied V2 would make the conservation assertion vacuous. The third — `phusdMinterMask` / `phusdMintVersion`, which story 076 promoted from a supporting record to the load-bearing input of the two-sided delta — has no such guard. `_snapshotPhusdMinterSet` (:974-997) returns early only when `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile` is already true; otherwise it records the LIVE mask unconditionally, with no reference to whether `p4e_v3_mintGrant` / `p4e_v2_mintRevoke` have already run. A `:resume` whose progress file lost the `baselines` block therefore stamps a post-cutover mask as the Phase 0 baseline and writes it straight back out; `VerifyPromotionReady._verifyMintAuthorityInvariance` then sees `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile == true` (:230-233 satisfied), compares live against a baseline taken from the same post-cutover state, and passes `liveMask == baseline & ~v2Bit` trivially — bit 19 is already clear on both sides after the revoke.
impact: A green `promotion-ready:verify` that proves nothing about the phUSD mint-authority delta — the single control story 076 added to replace story 072's now-false 'minter set byte-identical' invariant, and the one the operator is told (`:232`) is verified NOWHERE ELSE. It fails open, not closed. Reaching it requires an operator hand-trim error on the resume path, which the docs warn against in prose (`:800`, `:171-173`) — but the identical risk on the two sibling baselines was considered serious enough to guard in code, so the asymmetry is the defect.
evidence: side-effects.json.assertionCoverage.baselineGuards — a three-way comparison of the guards on `bptAtCutover`, `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover` (:798-801 deploy-side abort + :190-200 verifier abort) and `phusdMinterMask` (verifier abort at :230-233 only, no deploy-side abort). Prior art in the same ledger: L-02 `4fd1642310` ("Phase 7's BPT conservation assertion degrades to `>= 0` on every resume path") is the same class on a different baseline; this is disclosed as lineage, not presented as a fresh discovery — the mechanism differs (silent re-derivation of a post-state baseline vs. degradation to a zero baseline) and the affected control is new in story 076.
recommendation: Mirror :798-801 verbatim for the mint-authority baseline: in `_phase0_preconditions`, immediately after `_snapshotPhusdMinterSet()`, add `require(!(_isConfigured("p4e_v3_mintGrant") || _isConfigured("p4e_v2_mintRevoke")) || phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile, "RESUME ABORT: a phUSD setMinter step is already configured but the progress file carries no baselines.phusdMinterMask - restore that block verbatim; re-deriving it post-cutover makes the two-sided delta vacuous")`. Optionally also refuse to overwrite when `phusdMinterBaselineRecorded` would be taken after any Phase 4e mutation.

relatedFindings.relationship: ADDITIONAL LINEAGE ADDED BY SANITIZER (dedup disclosed only 4fd1642310). 80a741a27f (_parseBaselines: persisted baselines.bptAtCutover carries no provenance binding, a hand-edited digit is accepted) is the third member of the write-once-baseline family and is the closest structural neighbour after 4fd1642310. Still SEPARATE: 80a741a27f is about an UNVERIFIABLE persisted value on the bptAtCutover baseline; PR24-03 is about the ABSENCE of a resume abort on the phusdMinterMask baseline, so the value is silently RE-DERIVED post-cutover and then self-certifies. Different baseline, different mechanism, disjoint fixes. Disclosed, not collapsed.

classification.assetImpact: None directly. The loss is assurance: the verifier's phUSD mint-authority delta check can pass while proving nothing about the property it exists to prove.
attackPath: No attacker. Operator-error trigger with a non-obvious, fail-open consequence.
1. A :resume leg runs with a progress file whose `baselines` block was lost or hand-trimmed.

2. _snapshotPhusdMinterSet (:974-997) returns early only if phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile is already true; otherwise it records the LIVE mask unconditionally, with no reference to whether p4e_v3_mintGrant / p4e_v2_mintRevoke have already executed.
3. A POST-cutover mask is therefore stamped as the Phase 0 baseline and written back out.

4. VerifyPromotionReady._verifyMintAuthorityInvariance sees phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile == true (:230-233 satisfied) and compares live against a baseline drawn from the same post-cutover state, so `liveMask == baseline & ~v2Bit` passes trivially - bit 19 is already clear on both sides.
5. Operator reads a green verify for the one control the script tells them (:232) is verified nowhere else.
classification.likelihood: Low - requires a resume leg plus a damaged/trimmed progress file. But the project judged the identical risk serious enough to guard in code on both sibling baselines (bptAtCutover, phlimboV2StakedAtCutover at :798-801), so the exposure is an asymmetry, not an accepted design.
classification.assumptions: Assumes a resume path is taken and the baselines block is absent. Prose warnings at :800 and :171-173 exist but are not enforcement.
classification.externalRequirements: Operator hand-trim or loss of the progress file's baselines block.
classification.whyNotMedium: The verifier is an assurance surface, not a protocol function; a vacuous pass does not by itself move value or impair availability. Reaching it needs an operator file error that the two sibling baselines guard against. Medium would overstate.

justification: LOW. C4 QA/Low: state handling. Nothing is stolen, no protocol function is impaired - a control degrades to a tautology. Ranked first among the Lows because it fails OPEN on the single control story 076 added to replace story 072's now-false 'minter set byte-identical' invariant, and because the fix is a five-line mirror of an abort the codebase already writes twice.
regressionBasis: origin=new, carryoverOf=null, ledgerMatch=null, and the sanitizer's independent carryover re-check found no `fixed` entry matching this fingerprint. Not a regression.
severityHintDisposition: CONFIRMED at low after independent re-derivation; the hint was not accepted on trust. See justification.

knownIssueConsiderations.why: The trigger is an operator hand-trim of a progress file, but the harm is NON-OBVIOUS (the verifier goes green and self-certifies against a post-cutover baseline) and the project already guards the two sibling baselines in code (:798-801). Law 3 footgun test: a competent, non-malicious operator WOULD be surprised that a green verify proves nothing. In scope as an operational hazard. Not suppressed.

c4ValidityScreen: No known-invalid class applies. Not 'reckless admin mistake' — the harm is non-obvious and the two sibling baselines are guarded in code, so the asymmetry is the defect (Law 3 footgun exception).
dedupReasoning: Explicitly adjudicated per rule 3. Same CLASS (a write-once baseline unprotected across a resume leg), different defect on all four axes that matter: (1) different baseline — bptAtCutover vs phusdMinterMask; (2) different mechanism — L-02 DEGRADES the assertion to a vacuous `>= 0` against a zero baseline, PR24-03 SILENTLY RE-DERIVES a post-cutover baseline and then self-certifies against it, i.e. L-02 fails to prove while PR24-03 proves a tautology; (3) different control — the two-sided phUSD mint-authority delta is new in story 076 and did not exist when L-02 was filed, and the operator is told at :232 it is verified nowhere else; (4) different remediation — L-02 needs the BPT assertion to survive resume, PR24-03 needs a deploy-side RESUME ABORT mirroring :798-801, which would not touch the BPT path at all. Fixing L-02 leaves PR24-03 entirely live. NOT a carryover. Also checked against 80a741a27f (bptAtCutover provenance binding) — that is about a hand-edited VALUE being accepted, PR24-03 is about the ABSENCE of an abort when the block is missing; adjacent, not the same.
